title: Derived scalar comparisons are the specified invertible mates
statement:
Let $C_1\leftarrow C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be commutative rings and let $B$ be a commutative ring with compatible homomorphisms $B\to C_n$. On scheme pro-etale sites use $\mathscr S_X$, $\mathcal T_X$, and the exact sectionwise restriction $\rho_X^0$ with its ordinary normalized comparisons of [lem-sf-semilinear-scalar-ordinary-comparison]. Put $\rho_X=D(\rho_X^0)$. For every scheme map $f:X\to Y$, write $P_f\dashv S_f$ for the semilinear derived adjunction and $G_f\dashv R_f^{\mathcal T}$ for the constant-$B$ tower adjunction, using [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Exact localization gives $b_f:\rho_XP_f\cong G_f\rho_Y$. Define
$$d_f=(R_f^{\mathcal T}\rho_X\varepsilon_f)\circ(R_f^{\mathcal T}b_f^{-1}S_f)\circ(\eta_f^{\mathcal T}\rho_YS_f):\rho_YS_f\longrightarrow R_f^{\mathcal T}\rho_X,$$
thus $d_f$ is its specified adjunction mate. Then $d_f$ is an isomorphism and its evaluation at $n$ is the normalized ring-sheaf-change direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, exact localization of $a_j^0$ gives an isomorphism $a_j:\rho_XJ_j\cong J_j^{\mathcal T}\rho_U$ and its inverse is the left open-adjunction mate of $b_j$. For a commutative square $Q:pk=ir$ with $k:U\hookrightarrow V$, $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ quasi-compact open and $p:V\to Z$, $r:U\to W$ proper, these comparisons preserve the intrinsic $\alpha_Q$ before proper mating: after $b,a$ identify its domain and target, $\rho(\alpha_Q)=\alpha_Q^{\mathcal T}\rho$. These are equalities of specified system transformations; no faithfulness of derived evaluation is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary comparison to the given compatible maps $B\to C_n$. Its exact additive $\rho_T^0$ acts termwise on complexes, so it sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and defines $\rho_T$. The system inverse images are exact, and their derived functors are their localizations. Localize $b_f^0$ and its inverse using the natural-transformation part of the localization universal property; the two composites remain identities. This gives the specified $b_f:\rho_XP_f\cong G_f\rho_Y$. If $e^C_{T,n}$ and $e^B_{T,n}$ denote evaluation on the two system categories and $r_{T,n}$ single-level restriction from $C_n$ to $B$, then $e^B_{T,n}\rho_T=r_{T,n}e^C_{T,n}$, with the canonical localization identifications: both sides are the same termwise functor on complexes. The same localization uniqueness identifies the evaluation of $b_f$ with the ordinary inverse-image scalar comparison localized at level $n$.

proof.text:
Define $d_f$ by the displayed unit--$b_f^{-1}$--counit word, rather than choosing an isomorphism with its source and target. In the mate definition take $L_1=P_f$, $R_1=S_f$, $L_2=G_f$, $R_2=R_f^{\mathcal T}$, $G=\rho_Y$, $H=\rho_X$ and square $b_f^{-1}$. This gives exactly $d_f$. Here $\mathscr S_X$, the adjunction $P_f\dashv S_f$ and their level-$n$ evaluation comparisons are those of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]: evaluation of $P_f$ is the localized inverse-image comparison specified by the unit equation, and evaluation of $S_f$ is its adjunction mate. After the canonical identifications $f^{-1}(C_n)_Y\cong(C_n)_X$ of constant ring sheaves, these are the comparisons $e_nV=u^{-1}e_n$ and $e_nG\cong Ru_{*,n}e_n$ of the simultaneous system calculus for $u=f$, since a comparison compatible with the units and counits is the mate of the inverse-image comparison. Apply the evaluation comparisons of the simultaneous system calculus to both ring systems, using the constant ring system $B_n=\underline B$ for towers. They identify $e_nS_f$ and $e_nR_f^{\mathcal T}$ with the single-level derived direct images, and identify their units and counits. Together with step 1, evaluation of the actual word defining $d_f$ is therefore the single-level mate word
$$ (R_{f,B}r_{X,n}\varepsilon_{f,C_n})\circ(R_{f,B}b_{f,n}^{-1}R_{f,C_n})\circ(\eta_{f,B}r_{Y,n}R_{f,C_n}). $$
This is an application of the stated evaluation-of-transposes formula, including its unit and counit normalization.

proof.text: Apply the single-level ring-sheaf-change theorem to $u=f$, $R_T=\underline B_T$, $S_T=\underline {C_n}_T$, and $a_T$ induced by $B\to C_n$. The constant-coefficient inverse-image identifications of the tower calculus give $c_R,c_S$; the compatibility equation holds because both composites send a constant $b\in B$ to its image in $C_n$. Its inverse-image comparison is the one of step 1, since both are induced by identified-coefficient inverse image on module sheaves. In its adjunct equation put $M=R_{f,C_n}N$ and $t=\varepsilon_{f,C_n,N}$. Then $t^\sharp=1$ by the triangle identity. Consequently its specified direct-image comparison is the adjunct of $r_{X,n}(\varepsilon_{f,C_n,N})\circ b_{f,n,R_{f,C_n}N}^{-1}$. The mate formula identifies this adjunct with the word in step 2. Thus the evaluated $d_f$ is precisely that normalized comparison, and is invertible for every $n$ and every input.

proof.text: Apply joint detection of isomorphisms in the simultaneous-system theorem to the constant ring system $B_n=\underline B_Y$. Its semilinear category is exactly $\mathcal T_Y$, since restriction along the identity maps of $B$ is the identity. For every $N\in D(\mathscr S_X)$, step 3 says that every evaluation of $d_{f,N}$ is an isomorphism. Hence $d_{f,N}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal T_Y)$. The inverse components form a natural transformation by multiplying the naturality square of $d_f$ on both sides by these inverses, giving the asserted natural isomorphism. Only detection of invertibility has been used.

proof.text:
For the open $j$, localize $a_j^0$ and its inverse. All three functors involved are exact, including open extension, so localization gives an isomorphism $a_j:\rho_XJ_j\cong J_j^{\mathcal T}\rho_U$. Write $\eta^{o,C}$ for the unit of $J_j\dashv P_j$ and $\varepsilon^{o,B}$ for the counit of $J_j^{\mathcal T}\dashv G_j$. The left open-adjunction mate of $b_j$ is the map
$$\ell=(\varepsilon^{o,B}\rho_XJ_j)\circ(J_j^{\mathcal T}b_jJ_j)\circ(J_j^{\mathcal T}\rho_U\eta^{o,C}).$$
Already before deriving, normalization of $a_j^0$ by the open units states that the transpose of $(a_j^0)^{-1}$ is $b_j^0j_!\circ\rho_U^0\eta^{o,C}$. Applying the inverse adjunction bijection, or cancelling the adjacent unit and counit by the triangle identity, gives exactly the ordinary version of $\ell$. The open adjunctions descend with these ordinary units and counits by the system calculus. Localization respects composition and identities, so that equality descends to $\ell=a_j^{-1}$. This proves the left-mate assertion on systems.

proof.text:
Use the intrinsic ordinary $\alpha_Q$ and the ordinary scalar-comparison equation, not a proper mate or a levelwise identification. Its construction is the cartesian open comparison, the clopen projector, and the open and pullback compositors. The varying-ring-arrow definition localizes this very transformation; the tower calculus defines its constant-$B$ counterpart by the same exact operations. The ordinary comparison preserves the cartesian open comparison and projector and hence their full composite. Termwise application to complexes followed by localization, which respects composition, gives the explicit equation
$$(J_k^{\mathcal T}b_r)\circ(a_kP_r)\circ\rho_V(\alpha_Q)
=(\alpha_Q^{\mathcal T}\rho_W)\circ(G_pa_i)\circ(b_pJ_i).$$
Both sides run from $\rho_VP_pJ_i$ to $J_k^{\mathcal T}G_r\rho_W$. The hypotheses on $Q$ are exactly the proper/quasi-compact-open hypotheses of these intrinsic constructions, including the noncartesian case. This is the claimed equality after the specified $b,a$ identifications, before taking any proper mate. It is inherited from an equality of actual system transformations by localization, rather than inferred from evaluation.
